title: SignalR Hub + Real-time Messaging

criteria_checked.Two clients in same group receive messag: PASS (by code review + build - ChatHub.SendMessage broadcasts via Clients.Group("chat:{id}") to every connection that called JoinRoom, and AddStackExchangeRedis(DB 1) is wired so this fans out across replicas too; not live-tested against a running two-client WebSocket session, since bringing up the Docker stack is a user-run infra command per this project's convention - recommend validating with two SignalR clients after /docker-up as part of the QA checklist)
criteria_checked.Messages persisted to MongoDB before bro: PASS - ChatService.SendMessageAsync awaits IMessageRepository.CreateAsync(message) and returns the persisted MessageDto; ChatHub.SendMessage awaits that call and only then calls Clients.Group(...).SendAsync(...) - no parallel/fire-and-forget path
criteria_checked.GET /chats/:id/messages returns messages: PASS - MessageRepository.FindRecentByChatIdAsync sorts descending + Limit(n) at the query level to get the most recent N efficiently, then reverses the small result set to ascending order before returning

last_note: T036 complete: ChatHub (JoinRoom/SendMessage/LeaveRoom) + ChatController (GET messages, POST met) + IChatService layer shipped, SignalR Redis backplane on DB 1, dotnet build succeeds with 0 warnings/errors. Scope note: deliberately did NOT implement the OPEN/CLOSING/CLOSED state machine, grace timer, auto-close poller, connection.accepted consumer, or chat.closed Kafka/outbox publish - those are explicitly T037/T038/T039 per their own ticket files (already drafted in this repo). MarkMetSuccessfullyAsync only records each user's confirmation and returns both_users_met; a structured log line marks the hand-off point for T037/T039 to pick up, per T036's own 'do not implement the full saga' scope note.
